text:
incident-bot: PAGED rachel (oncall): ALERT: possible cross-customer KV visibility detected for customer ELYSIUM in dedicated pool us-east-2a. Severity: P1 - potential data exposure. Source: automated kvcache-health check. Please ack and assemble triage.

rachel (oncall): acked. joining. @maya @devon will look. sam please stand by for customer comms.

maya (sre): on it. first quick questions: do we have evidence showing reads of ELYSIUM-prefixed keys on nodes not assigned to their VPC? any timeframe?

incident-bot: Evidence artifact uploaded: https://internal.redwood/artefacts/2609876543/elysium-kv-reads.log (contains anonymized key prefixes and node ids).

maya (sre): grabbing logs now. snippet:
```
[us-east-2a-node-47] read key=elysium:session:0x9f3a from kvcache (owner_vpc=elysium-vpc)
[us-east-2a-node-12] read key=elysium:session:0x9f3a from kvcache (owner_vpc=public-dedicated)
```
Looks like same key observed on node-12 which should be in a different VPC tenancy group.

devon (infra): that node-12 was part of last-night maintenance for pool rebalancing. we did a live node swap to add capacity to us-east-2a dedicated clusters at 03:12 UTC. may be related. I will pull the orchestration events.

alex (eng): quick hypothesis: latebind sticky KV prefixes + a bug in the eviction metadata caused prefix ownership not to clear on node swap. if true, reads could be served from stale cache entries until TTL/eviction triggers.

sam (support): drafting an initial customer note for ELYSIUM (DO NOT SEND)
> Hi team, we detected anomalous behavior in the dedicated pool serving your workspace. We're investigating and have isolated the affected capacity. We'll provide an update within 60 minutes. Apologies for the disruption.

rachel (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) cordon us-east-2a dedicated pool (prevent new allocations) 2) run targeted kvcache flush on nodes that were part of the swap 3) audit read/writes and capture any possible lateral reads 4) coordinate a short customer-facing update. I'll execute 1 and 2 now.

rachel (oncall): running command to cordon pool:
```
$ radmin pool cordon us-east-2a-dedicated --reason "kvcache-ownership-anomaly"
```

ops-bot: Pool us-east-2a-dedicated cordoned by rachel at 2609876562. No new allocations will be scheduled.

rachel (oncall): running targeted cache flush on node-12 and node-47:
```
$ infractl kvcache flush --nodes node-12,node-47 --prefix "elysium:" --force
```

ops-bot: kvcache flush started (job id: kf-2609876570). Progress: node-12: queued -> running, node-47: queued -> running.

maya (sre): while flush runs, I pulled additional logs for cross-check. query: count of distinct nodeIDs that served keys with prefix elysium: in last 24h -> 3 distinct nodes, timestamps clustered around 03:10-03:30 UTC (near maintenance window). Suspicious.

devon (infra): orchestration events show node-12 was briefly attached to a different tenant group due to a metadata reconciliation race:
```
2026-09-12T03:11:52Z: attach node-12 -> pool us-east-2a-dedicated
2026-09-12T03:12:05Z: set node-12 tenancy=public-dedicated
2026-09-12T03:12:06Z: reconcile tenancy meta -> inconsistent write (retry)
```
Looks like a window where tenancy tags were inconsistent.

alex (eng): can we confirm whether the kvcache keys carry owner-vpc tokens in metadata? if they do, why did node-12 serve the key? either the owner token wasn't checked on read (bug) or the cached entry lacked owner metadata. both are bad.

maya (sre): confirmed: some cached entries for elysium keys have owner_vpc=null on node-12 snapshot. So the cache entry lost owner metadata during reassign.

alex (eng): ok root cause candidate = metadata-strip on cache entries during node reassign + orchestration race. Immediate mitigations: a) finish targeted flush b) block read-from-cache for elysium prefix until audit completes (cheap) c) rotate per-tenant cache prefixes (longer).

rachel (oncall): implementing b) now (disable read from kvcache for prefixes matching elysium):
```
$ runtimectl feature-toggle disable-kvcache-read --prefix "elysium:"
```

ops-bot: disable-kvcache-read for prefix 'elysium:' applied at 2609876610.

maya (sre): flush job kf-2609876570 completed: node-12 cleared, node-47 cleared. scanning historical reads for lateral access. preliminary result: no reads beyond the 3 nodes found; no evidence of bulk list/dump. still analyzing full trace.

sam (support): updated customer message (DRAFT):
> We found and isolated an anomaly in the dedicated pool that may have allowed temporary cache visibility across nodes during a maintenance window. We cordoned the pool and flushed affected cache entries. No evidence so far of broad data leakage. We will follow up with a full report within 24 hours.

devon (infra): recommendation: rollback the latebind reassign for the three nodes until we push a fix to ensure owner metadata is preserved across reassign. I can run a scheduled rollback if oncall agrees.

alex (eng): +1 rollback. also queue a postmortem and a code patch to assert owner_vpc present on cache write and fail-fast otherwise. add an integration test for node reassign flow.

rachel (oncall): OK I'm initiating a controlled rollback of the node reassign for node-12 via orchestration (will do in 5m with maintenance window). After rollback, we'll re-enable kvcache reads for elysium if scans look clean.

ops-bot: orchestration rollback job rb-2609876740 started. ETA ~120s.

maya (sre): post-rollback quick-check: node allocations stable; no new lateral reads seen after disable and flush. full trace scan still running, ETA ~18m.

rachel (oncall): handoff to alex (next oncall) at 2609876899. Summary for handoff:
- Incident: suspected kvcache ownership metadata loss during node reassign in us-east-2a dedicated pool (customer ELYSIUM).
- Actions taken: pool cordoned, targeted kvcache flush, disabled kvcache reads for elysium:, orchestration rollback started, preliminary audit shows 3 nodes involved, no evidence of broad exfiltration.
- Open items: full trace audit, permanent fix for owner_vpc write guard, integration test for reassign, customer postmortem + formal 24h report.

alex (eng): taking over. I'll keep the channel updated and drive the postmortem and fix prioritization. Please push any remaining artifacts to the incident folder: /incidents/2609876543/artifacts.

sam (support): will send the 60-min follow-up to ELYSIUM now with the current mitigations and ETA for full report.

rachel (oncall): thanks team. tagging this as "oncall-handoff" and moving to monitoring. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: PAGER CLEAR for rachel at 2609876899 (handed to alex).
